name: Ho Chi Minh City
provinceNote: A centrally run city. Since 1 July 2025 it includes the former Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and Bình Dương. The walkable center is still the old core.
summary: Former Saigon in the south, with the cathedral square, Japanese alleys, and Chợ Lớn. Walk Nguyễn Huệ at sundown, eat in the Japanese alleys off Lê Thánh Tôn and Thái Văn Lung, and walk the shophouse streets of the Chinese quarter in District 5.
timeNeeded: Long enough for the old core, a half-day in Chợ Lớn, and a side trip to Củ Chi or the Mekong.
fee: Palace from 1 Aug 2025: palace-only adult 40,000 đồng; palace-plus-exhibition 80,000 đồng; homepage adult 80,000 đồng; older attractions line 15,000 đồng. Museum from 1 Oct 2026: adult 60,000 đồng; older attractions line 15,000 đồng. Pupils and students: a free online ticket on the museum page, not a half-price row. Metro fares in the Dec 2024 opening article: 6,000–20,000 đồng a ride, plus day and month passes in that article. Not a 2026 price. Fare now: Check on arrival. Bus fare: Check on arrival. City counts: 6,772.59 km² and 14,002,598 people; April 2025 proposal 6,772.65 km² and 13,706,632 people; nearly 9 million.
getThere: Tân Sơn Nhất is 7 km from the centre, with taxis, ride-hailing, and city buses. Metro Line 1 runs from Bến Thành to Bến xe Suối Tiên, about 19.7 km, 14 stations, a 29-minute ride in the December 2024 opening article, initial clock 05:00–22:00. A visitor line names Bến xe Miền Đông as the eastern end. Rush hours 7:00–9:00 and 16:30–18:30. More than 150 bus routes, plus the Saigon Waterbus and public bicycles.
seoTitle: Ho Chi Minh City travel guide — street food, Ben Thanh, War Remnants Museum
seoDescription: Eat cơm tấm and bánh mì, walk Bến Thành and the cathedral square, and see the war record at the War Remnants Museum. Tân Sơn Nhất is 7 km from the centre. After dark the motorbikes are still on Bùi Viện.
intro: You step onto Nguyễn Huệ at sundown, motorbikes threading the colonial core, the walking street running from City Hall down toward Bạch Đằng, and the cathedral’s twin spires at the head of Đồng Khởi with the post office opposite.

Many residents still say Sài Gòn. The city’s history runs a little more than 300 years, and the old name is still in daily use. The walkable center is the old core, even after the 2025 merger. City Hall is not open to the public. Eat cơm tấm and hủ tiếu on the street, then bánh mì. Phở is the bowl that belongs in Hanoi. Hủ tiếu is the one that belongs here.

Bến Thành is the market hall on the square, food stalls at the end of the aisle. The Reunification Palace and the War Remnants Museum hold the war record. Chợ Lớn is the Chinese quarter in District 5, at Bình Tây and Thiên Hậu. The Japanese alleys are on Lê Thánh Tôn and Thái Văn Lung. After dark, Bùi Viện crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão, Đề Thám, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu.
gettingAround: Tân Sơn Nhất is the airport, 7 km from the centre. Taxis, ride-hailing, and city buses cover that ride. Cross with a slow, steady pace. Rush hours are 7:00–9:00 and 16:30–18:30.

Metro Line 1 is running, from Bến Thành toward the east: Bến xe Suối Tiên on the project page and the December 2024 opening article, about 19.7 km and 14 stations, with a 29-minute ride and an initial clock of 05:00–22:00. Bến xe Miền Đông is the eastern end on the visitor line. The same visitor page names the Saigon Waterbus, public bicycles, and more than 150 bus routes.

stayAreas.name: Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ
stayAreas.summary: A room within a walk of Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ puts the cathedral, the post office, and the sundown street outside the door. Bùi Viện is the other night, where it crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão, Đề Thám, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu.

eat: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, bánh mì, bánh xèo, gỏi cuốn, and cà phê sữa đá are the plates to start with. This city mixes regions. Phở is best in Hanoi.
The food guide is the streets, the doors, and the three fine-dining rooms.
interestsBody: Street food first, then the cathedral square, the war record, Chợ Lớn, and Bến Thành. Sidewalk coffee is a glass on the pavement.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Cơm tấm is the essential plate here. Hủ tiếu is the bowl that belongs in this city.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, the snail streets, and the three fine-dining rooms.

interestGroups.title: Dong Khoi and the cathedral square
interestGroups.summary: The twin-spired cathedral at the head of Đồng Khởi, the post office opposite, the opera along the street, and Nguyễn Huệ at sundown.

cards.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral
cards.summary: Both towers and the rose window. The post office is the building opposite.

cards.title: Opera House
cards.summary: The facade on Đồng Khởi. A night show is a separate ticket.

cards.title: Nguyen Hue
cards.summary: The walking street from City Hall to Bạch Đằng, liveliest at sundown.

interestGroups.title: The war record
interestGroups.summary: The palace on Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa and the museum on Võ Văn Tần.

blocks.heading: The palace and the museum
paragraphs: Walk the palace halls on the old Norodom site, then the basement command center. The ticket has more than one adult line, so read the desk before you pay.
The museum is three floors of artifacts and photographs, and aircraft in the courtyard. Pupils and students use a free online ticket.

cards.title: Reunification Palace
cards.summary: The halls on the old Norodom site, and the basement command center.

cards.title: War Remnants Museum
cards.summary: Three floors of artifacts and photographs, and aircraft in the courtyard.

interestGroups.title: Cho Lon
interestGroups.summary: The Chinese neighborhood to walk. Bình Tây and Thiên Hậu are the halls. Chợ Lớn stays an area of this city.

cards.title: Binh Tay Market
cards.summary: The wholesale hall in Chợ Lớn. The gate carries the clock and the name.

cards.title: Thien Hau Temple
cards.summary: The hall of Thiên Hậu in Chợ Lớn, dated to 1760.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Bến Thành faces Quách Thị Trang, souvenirs in the aisle and food at the end of the hall. Vincom Center and Saigon Centre–Takashimaya sit with the walking streets.

cards.title: Ben Thanh Market
cards.summary: The clock tower and the name, on the square where the metro station sits. Souvenirs in the aisle, food stalls at the end of the hall.

cards.title: Vincom Center Dong Khoi
cards.summary: The mall named with Saigon Centre–Takashimaya. The signs in the frame read Lê Thánh Tôn and Đồng Khởi.

blocks.heading: Ben Thanh Market
paragraphs: The clock tower and the name sit on the square where the metro station is. The aisle is souvenirs. The food stalls are at the end of the hall.
Chợ Tân Định is the Sunday morning market on Hai Bà Trưng, in District 3. Saigon Centre–Takashimaya is named with Vincom Center on the walking streets, at the Lê Thánh Tôn and Đồng Khởi signs.

interestGroups.title: Sidewalk coffee
interestGroups.summary: Cà phê sữa đá in the park outside the palace, and the sidewalk glass at Turtle Lake.

cards.title: Cà phê sữa đá
cards.summary: The Saturday morning cup outside the palace, and cloth-filter coffee on the sidewalk.

faqs.q: Is Ho Chi Minh City the same as Saigon?
faqs.a: Many residents still say Sài Gòn. Ho Chi Minh City is the official name. Since 1 July 2025 the city includes the former Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and Bình Dương. The center you walk is the old core.
Counts in use are 6,772.59 km² and 14,002,598 people, 6,772.65 km² and 13,706,632 people, and nearly 9 million. The walkable center is still the old core. There is no single published map pin.

Cơm tấm is the go-to breakfast and also an any-meal plate. Bánh mì starts a morning. Cà phê sữa đá is the Saturday cup in the park outside the palace. Chợ Tân Định is the Sunday morning market on Hai Bà Trưng, in District 3.

season.label: Drier from December to April
season.note: December to April is drier, sunny, and less humid. May to November brings short afternoon showers. It is hot all year.
